clue.text: Grate pickle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rub harshly against a surface
second meaning: an awkward fix or predicament

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a kitchen instruction to shred a gherkin; in fact both words are separate meanings of one word, a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for rubbing harshly and a noun for a tricky predicament, matching each half of the clue.

clue.text: Wrong dose ain't calming someone down

indicators.note: a wrong arrangement is one out of its proper order, so the letters must be put right

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A wrongly measured dose has failed to settle an agitated patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedation is the process of calming a person with drugs, which is what calming someone down describes.

clue.text: What's left in reserve, I expected

parts.note: RES is a standard abbreviation for reserve
taken as written
something due is expected to arrive

explanation.surface: Someone guessed there would be something kept back in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is the remainder of something after the rest has gone, so it is the part still left over.

clue.text: Maybe he's topping cake with no filling, say

parts.note: he is an example of a part of speech that stands for a noun

indicators.note: a word with its filling gone keeps only its outside letters, the middle removed

parts.note: just the first and last letters of cake

explanation.surface: Perhaps a man is putting a sponge with no jam or cream on top of something.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'topping' puts the first piece above the second. 'Maybe' signals that he is just one example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to utter or declare, so it is a synonym of the verb say.

clue.text: Broad smile initially, then visibly upset?

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word before it is taken

parts.note: first letter of smile
someone shedding tears is visibly upset

explanation.surface: A face that begins with a wide grin and then crumples into tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broad smile' reads as one phrase, but Broad is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeping statement or change is broad and wide-ranging in scope, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: County doctors were choristers

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: In some English county, the local doctors used to sing in a church choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is a verb telling you to rework the letters. Worcestershire is a county in the English West Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Worcestershire is one of the historic shire counties of England, so it is an example of a county.

clue.text: Polish off attack having dispensed with leader

indicators.note: getting rid of the leader means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to beat up someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: An army finishes off its assault after getting rid of its commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' tempts with the nationality, but it is the verb in the phrase polish off.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish off food is to consume all of it, which is what the phrasal verb means too.

clue.text: Tick in street, tiny creature

parts.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street
an ant is a tiny insect

explanation.surface: A tick, a small bloodsucker, spotted on the road among other little creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: Tick suggests the parasite, which fits the tiny creature; here it means a moment, as in 'just a tick'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British speech a tick is a very short moment of time, the same sense as an instant.

clue.text: An article supporting fellow somewhere in South America

indicators.note: in a down clue, what supports something sits beneath it, so the article pair is placed second

parts.note: a guy is a man or fellow
taken as written
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece backing a man who lives somewhere on the South American continent.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts the second part beneath the first, so the fellow goes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Guyana is a country on the north-east coast of South America, so it is a place on that continent.

clue.text: One floored by cleaner? That's painful

definitions.text: One floored by cleaner? That's painful

parts.note: surface reading: someone knocked to the ground by a domestic cleaner
setter's reading: a sore joint caused by a domestic servant kneeling on the floor to scrub it

explanation.walkthrough: Floored suggests being knocked down, but the cleaner is literally on the floor, kneeling to scrub. The condition named after her is an inflamed knee.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the common name for prepatellar bursitis, a painful swelling caused by long kneeling, once typical of servants scrubbing floors.

clue.text: Mark joins club with scowl

parts.note: a disco is a nightclub for dancing
to lour is to frown or look sullen

explanation.surface: A man called Mark signs up to a club and frowns about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a man's name; here it is a verb meaning to stain.
explanation.definitionFit: To discolour something is to stain or blemish it, which is one sense of the verb to mark.

clue.text: Inviting contempt in the end, a dirty abode

indicators.note: the end of the word is its final letter, the only one that is used

parts.note: last letter of contempt
taken as written
a pigsty is a filthy dwelling

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that a grubby home is asking for scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: Inviting seems to go with contempt, but it stands alone as the definition, meaning appetising.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasty food is appealing and appetising, so it is inviting in the sense of tempting the palate.

clue.text: Uninspired outside right? No!

indicators.note: if the letters are not right they are wrong, so they need to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dull football winger, the outside right, is scorned by the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The outside right is an old football position on the right wing; the phrase breaks apart, with 'right? No!' meaning wrong, the letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tedious is dull and lacking flair, which is what uninspired means.

clue.text: Justify first of ideas in ditched strategy?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the following one

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, someone ditched
a plan is a strategy

indicators.note: first of points to the opening letter alone of the following word

parts.note: first letter of ideas

explanation.surface: A manager is asked to defend an idea that was part of an abandoned strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: EX, meaning former or discarded, stands before the strategy, which has the first letter of ideas tucked inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain an action is to give reasons for it, which is to justify it.

clue.text: Composition being shown in cinema

parts.note: an ode is a poetic composition
a film that is on is being shown

explanation.surface: A musical piece is screened at the local picture house.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon is a well-known chain of British cinemas, and the name came to stand for a picture house generally.

clue.text: Change around odd bits of loin, sent back for butcher

indicators.note: around means the first word wraps itself about the other piece

parts.note: to mutate is to change

indicators.note: something sent back goes the opposite way, so read the letters right to left
the odd-numbered letters are the first, third and so on, which are the ones kept

parts.note: first and third letters of loin

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to prepare a cut of meat: swap bits of the loin around for the butcher.
explanation.walkthrough: Butcher looks like the person at the shop counter; it is the verb, meaning to hack about.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutilate is to damage savagely by cutting, which is what butcher means as a verb.

clue.text: A strip under bottom of small washer

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter, the only one used

parts.note: last letter of small
taken as written
to strip is to take off one's clothes

explanation.surface: A thin strip of rubber fitted under a small washer, as in plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' sets the strip below the small piece in a down entry. Washer suggests a plumbing ring, but it means a person who washes.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman employed to wash clothes and linen, so she is a washer of laundry.

clue.text: Private parking north of New Orleans

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the following word is reshaped into another order

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
letters of Orleans in a new order

explanation.surface: A private parking area just north of the city of New Orleans.
explanation.walkthrough: New Orleans reads as one city name, but New is split off to rework the letters. 'North of' places the P above in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal matters are private ones, concerning one person rather than the public.

clue.text: Exciting story embraced by Queen, accommodating type?

parts.note: a hot story is an exciting one

indicators.note: being embraced means being held inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina
a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: A sensational tale embraced by the monarch, who is being obliging.
explanation.walkthrough: Accommodating suggests obliging, but the hotel keeper provides accommodation; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotelier runs a hotel, providing rooms and lodging for guests, so the pun on accommodation fits.

clue.text: Boaters in Ransome novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the name's letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Children messing about in boats in an Arthur Ransome book such as Swallows and Amazons.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like a book by the children's author Arthur Ransome, but it is an adjective signalling the rearrangement. Boaters may suggest straw hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Oarsmen row boats, so they are boaters in the sense of people who go boating.

clue.text: Relative idiot scratching head having bagged first in Latin

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it in a bag, so one piece is held inside another
scratching out the head removes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a dunce is a slow learner, an idiot

indicators.note: first in means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: first letter of Latin

explanation.surface: A dim family member scratches their head after scraping through a Latin exam.
explanation.walkthrough: Once the dunce loses its first letter, what remains wraps around the initial of Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a family member, a parent's brother, so he is a relative.

clue.text: Dessert that's superior, cold inside

indicators.note: inside means the short piece sits within the longer word

parts.note: choice goods are of superior quality
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A posh chilled pudding with a cold centre.
explanation.walkthrough: A choc ice is a British ice-cream bar coated in chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: A choc ice is a frozen sweet eaten after a meal or as a treat, so it is a kind of dessert.

clue.text: Powerful businessmen working in pubs

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the following word

parts.note: bars are places to drink, like pubs
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Tycoons who do their deals over drinks in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrial magnates are often called barons, as in press barons, a figurative use of the noble title.

clue.text: Close, don't open without locks

indicators.note: if the word may not open, its opening letter is taken away

parts.note: locks are hair, so without them is bald

explanation.surface: Instructions to shut a door that cannot be opened because it has no locks.
explanation.walkthrough: Close looks like the verb shut, matching the doors and locks; it is the adjective for muggy weather, pronounced with a soft S.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather is humid and stuffy, lacking fresh air, which is exactly what airless means.

clue.text: Located in file, the registration number

indicators.note: located in says the word sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of file, all of the, and the start of registration

explanation.surface: A vehicle's registration number found in a filing record.
explanation.walkthrough: Number looks like a digit, but read it as 'numb-er': something that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was an early anaesthetic, so it is something that makes people numb.

clue.text: Horrible secret locations: time to escape!

indicators.note: a letter that escapes has got out, so it is removed from the word

parts.note: hideouts are secret places to lie low
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Fugitives in a grim hiding place decide it is time to break out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hideous is very ugly or dreadful, which matches horrible as a synonym.

clue.text: Energy member invested in expression of surprise

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: ooh is a cry of surprise
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician puts real drive into a gasp of astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is an informal word for vigour and zest, so it is a synonym of energy.

clue.text: European anger now, I suspect

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious or unsound, so the letters are not in their proper order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a person from Europe is now feeling furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I suspect' reads as a hedge; only suspect is the signal, and the I is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norwegian is a person from Norway, a country in Europe, so is an example of a European.

clue.text: So, perhaps rain wets various things?

indicators.note: a hint that the picture painted is to be flipped, each word swapped for its contrary

parts.note: the opposite kind of weather to rain
the opposite action to wetting

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek remark that rain dampens all sorts of things.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual clue of contraries: swap rain and wets for their opposites and the phrase that results, read as one word, is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundries are miscellaneous small items, odds and ends, so they are assorted things of many kinds.

clue.text: A mushroom with the other ingredients?

parts.note: taken as written
to mushroom is to grow rapidly, to swell

explanation.surface: A recipe asks whether a mushroom goes in along with everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: Mushroom looks like a food among the ingredients; it is a verb meaning grow fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in addition or too, so an item added as well goes in along with the other ingredients.
